findings.location: crosswalk.json papers[7] (MASS 2502.02533).status; papers[5] (Harness-Zero 2609.24974).status; papers[1] (VeriHarness) codeAvailability, grounding.claims[8].finding and upstreams[veriharness].what; short names and findings citing authors
findings.finding: The public record carries personal data that the design says is not recorded. The MASS status gives the two corresponding authors' e-mail addresses in obfuscated '<user> at <domain>' form, and names a third person together with their student-researcher role. The Harness-Zero status ends with the corresponding author's full name. Both come verbatim from the grounding records' venue_or_status, which the builder copies with .strip() only. This review deliberately does not repeat those values. Lower-order: a personal Hugging Face account handle appears three times in the rollout-corpus URL, and author surnames appear in citation form: the short names of 2512.08296 and 2607.12227 use 'Surname et al.', two 'Surname et al., year' citations sit inside VeriHarness and MASS findings, and one bare surname sits in an Agensh finding. README.md does not carry the status fields; the overlap is in crosswalk.json only. No local user names, home-directory paths, account names of the operator or real e-mail addresses (with '@') were found in either file.
findings.requiredChange: Remove names, e-mail addresses (including obfuscated 'x at domain' forms) and personal roles from every seed status. Have the builder emit venue/version/date only rather than copying venue_or_status. Decide on citation-style surnames and the dataset-URL handle: either replace them with titles or arXiv ids, or have the owner accept them as an explicit exception and say so in nonClaims and the README. Add a checker hygiene rule that rejects '@', the '<word> at <domain>.<tld>' pattern, 'corresponding author' and home-directory paths in every string.

findings.location: crosswalk.json critique[2] (CE-3).figure and README 'Critique evidence' CE-3 row (builder CRITIQUE constant)
findings.finding: CE-3 says that under a fixed executor 'only one of five lineages improves held-out'. HarnessDev p.11 (Sec 4.3), Table 6 p.12 and p.13 report five self-runtime lineages plus four fixed-Gemini ablations (Opus, Qwen, DeepSeek, GPT-5.5). Under fixed Gemini only Opus improves (+2.70) and the other three regress (-1.11, -2.38, -10.32), so the correct count is one of four. The rest of the row matches the PDF: feedback-pair gains +3.0 to +13.9, held-out +1.43 to +4.44, and 2 clear positives out of 64 switches. The grounding record (claim 6 finding) has the correct statement; the error was introduced in the builder's hand-written CRITIQUE text.
findings.requiredChange: Change to 'under the fixed Gemini executor only one of four lineages (Opus, +2.70) improves held-out; the other three regress, down to -10.32' and regenerate the README.

findings.location: crosswalk.json papers[0..7].grounding.claims[].claim and claimCounts; README 'Seed papers' lead sentence; checker SEED_CLAIMS
findings.finding: The claims list mixes claims the syntheses made with availability and licence checks, and it keeps leftover grounding-prompt instructions. All six NOT_FOUND rows are checks of whether code or a licence is available, not synthesis claims the papers fail to support: HERMES 6, MILO 7, Agensh 8, Harness-Zero 8, HarnessDev 8 and MASS 8. About 19 claim texts carry instructions or check wording, for example 'name the benchmarks and the models', '(give the numbers)', '(or whatever the paper names)', '(Apache-2.0?)', 'if stated' and '(exact list)', and numbering prefixes are inconsistent ('1.', '7a.'). The README says 'Every claim the syntheses attributed to a seed paper was checked against the PDF', so the 50/4/6 tally reads as six unsupported synthesis claims.
findings.requiredChange: Tag each row with a kind (SYNTHESIS_CLAIM, or AVAILABILITY_OR_LICENCE_CHECK / VENUE_CHECK), or split the checks out. Strip the prompt residue and numbering prefixes from the claim texts; the grounding digest keeps provenance. Restate the tally per kind in the record and the README, and update the checker constant to match.

findings.finding: Codebase text copied from the roadmap defers work 'to MAS-RA-000', which is this record, and so contradicts the record's own outcome. The llm-as-a-verifier caveat says 'locate and licence-check at MAS-RA-000'. The agensh caveat says 'Re-check at MAS-RA-000; until then the paper is the reference', although the re-check ran. The harnessdev caveat says 're-check at MAS-RA-000'. The jaz 'what' gives the reason jaz-evals was not checked as 'GitHub rate limit', while OI-1 gives it as outside the approved pass. An open item is also missing: the VENDOR_CANDIDATE veriharness lists the released rollout corpus (a Hugging Face dataset) 'as fixtures'. The policy sets datasetLicenseApprovalRequired: true, and the roadmap's MAS-RA-000 grounding note says the upstream record must carry the licence check. The dataset was outside Q-RA1 and its licence is unchecked, yet no OI records that. OI-5 cites 'handoff section 7', an internal document that is not in this public repository.
findings.requiredChange: Rewrite the four stale strings so they state the 2026-10-12 outcome and point to OI-2, OI-4, OI-3 and OI-1. Add an OI-7 for the rollout-corpus dataset licence, carried to MAS-RA-001 and MAS-RA-002. Make OI-5 self-contained, for example 'open owner choice, recorded in the roadmap'.

findings.location: scripts/research_adoption_v2.py classify(), DEFAULT_ALLOWED..DENIED constants, LICENSE_BLOCKED rule; builder classify()
findings.finding: The checker claims to implement 'the lists the outcome is computed from' in policy 0.3.0 but omits two of them: allowedExceptionExpressions (ALLOWED_EXCEPTION_EXPRESSION) and optionalExplicitReview (OPTIONAL_EXPLICIT_REVIEW). It also ignores the precedence and mixed-set rules. In the mutation probe, a GPL-3.0-only repository labelled OPTIONAL_EXPLICIT_REVIEW (correct under the policy) is rejected, while the same repository labelled DENY_UNKNOWN_LICENSE (wrong) is accepted. The LICENSE_BLOCKED rule also rejects a DENY_UNKNOWN_LICENSE outcome. The 40 current records are classified correctly.
findings.requiredChange: Implement every list in the pinned policy, with its precedence, or make classify() fail closed on any identifier outside the implemented lists rather than returning DENY_UNKNOWN_LICENSE. Allow LICENSE_BLOCKED with DENY_UNKNOWN_LICENSE and OPTIONAL_EXPLICIT_REVIEW. Mirror the change in the builder.

findings.location: crosswalk.json (no reuseModes / alignmentRule), README Codebases and Seed papers sections; checker reuse-mode rules
findings.finding: The record and README use reuse modes REFERENCE_DESIGN..NOT_APPLICABLE and alignment classes ADOPTION_CANDIDATE / CONCEPTUAL_ALIGNMENT without defining them. The definitions sit only in roadmap.json research.reuseModes, and the predecessor uses a different pair (CONCEPTUAL_ALIGNMENT / EVALUATED_COMPONENT). designReferenceOnly is a ceiling derived from the licence, so it is False for REFERENCE_DESIGN and INDEX_ONLY repositories under MIT or Apache, which is easy to misread as clearance. The checker enforces the reuse-mode rules in one direction only. The mutation probe accepted: TEST_ORACLE_CANDIDATE with DENY_MISSING_LICENSE or DENIED; NOT_APPLICABLE or NOT_RETRIEVABLE on a repository that was found; and PLANNED_BASELINE with an empty predecessorMapMention ('' is a substring of any text).
findings.requiredChange: Add reuseModes and alignmentRule definitions, plus the meaning of designReferenceOnly, to the record and README. In the checker: NOT_APPLICABLE only when there is no repository; NOT_RETRIEVABLE only when found is false; TEST_ORACLE_CANDIDATE only with DEFAULT_ALLOWED, or OPEN_CONTENT for non-code fixtures; PLANNED_BASELINE only with DEFAULT_ALLOWED or PLANNED_UNRESOLVED; predecessorMapMention must be non-empty text.

findings.location: scripts/research_adoption_v2.py (decisions, PAGE_REF, README coverage, parser, field typing)
findings.finding:
Other checker gaps found by the mutation probe:
(a) Owner decision texts are not pinned. Q-RA1 and Q-RA2 can be rewritten to anything, and HO-D1..D3 only need their id prefix, although the record presents them as verbatim.
(b) PAGE_REF accepts 'p95 latency' as a page citation.
(c) README coverage only checks that names are present. A changed table row (veriharness shown as LICENSE_BLOCKED / DENY_MISSING_LICENSE with a zero commit) and a missing MCP standards row both pass.
(d) The pdf key set is open, and statusDetail is not validated (an empty string passes).
(e) packetCheck stars, pushedAt and license are not type-checked, roadmapCheck values are not checked, and 1e999 (parsed as infinity) is accepted.
(f) metaBase is not pinned to 93d32e1.
(g) A record nested 100k levels deep, which is under 4 MiB, escapes as RecursionError; a missing record or README escapes as FileNotFoundError. The brief requires ValueError only.
The checker uses the standard library only (hashlib, json, re), makes no network call, and reads only through the injected reader. The task-packets path is built from a value already matched by PACKET_ID.
findings.requiredChange: Pin the decision texts by exact value or digest; tighten PAGE_REF to the p./pp. forms used; check README rows against a deterministic rendering of the record (or compare the README to that rendering byte for byte); close pdf; type-check statusDetail and the packetCheck/roadmapCheck fields and reject non-finite numbers; pin metaBase; convert RecursionError, and OSError on a required read, into ValueError.

findings.location: judgement calls (alignment, standards, secondary rows, CC0, Langfuse, OI-1..OI-6, overlay)
findings.finding:
Successor overlay: agree. 25 repository files pin the predecessor digest and architecture/unified-roadmap-authority.json pins the map, so an in-place amendment is not possible. The relation text and README describe the split correctly, and the policies equal the predecessor's.
Alignment rule (ADOPTION_CANDIDATE only through a VENDOR_CANDIDATE codebase): agree.
CC0-1.0 code (claudes-c-compiler) as a design reference only: agree. The policy's OPEN_CONTENT allowedUse covers non-code content only and osiApprovedOnly applies to code, so add a licenseNote saying that.
Langfuse as PLANNED_BASELINE with PLANNED_UNRESOLVED: agree. plannedUnresolvedRule allows a PLANNED placeholder with DENY_RELEASE, and the map lists 'Langfuse OSS later' under H15 'Later coverage'.
OI-1..OI-3 outside the 41-repository pass: agree.
Standards: agree, but suggest MCP also map to H11 and MAS-RA-008, since its role says 'behind the tool gateway'.
Secondary rows: the items match the MAS-RA item texts. Two harness rows leave a declared layer without a harness: RLM (L1, L2) has only H10, and AggAgent (L3, L4) has only H16. Suggest adding H8 or H7, and H10.
Secondary names mix two sources. 2607.12227 drops 'for Agents', and AHE, DeLM and MAST use the Part A labels while the others use full titles.
VeriHarness claim 5 ('hit rate' against a token share) and JAZ claim 3 (far-recall subset only) are VERIFIED with material qualifications. State the status rubric.
The roadmap's MAS-RA-000 deliverables still describe an in-place amendment. The roadmap session should restate them at adoption.
findings.requiredChange: None required. Optional: the licenseNote for claudes-c-compiler, the MCP H11/MAS-RA-008 mapping, RLM/AggAgent harness rows, consistent secondary titles, and a stated status rubric.
